title: connect_ws: uppercase WS:// bypasses scheme guard, yields WebSocket err not InvalidArgument
description: connect_ws checks starts_with("ws://") and starts_with("wss://") (lowercase only). A URL "WS://host/" or "WSS://host/" does not match either prefix, so the function falls through to into_client_request(), which returns a tungstenite error (ClientError::WebSocket) rather than ClientError::InvalidArgument. The doc comment says 'Returns ClientError::InvalidArgument if the URL scheme is not ws:// or wss://', but that contract is violated for uppercase-scheme inputs. The SSRF guard is then also absent for uppercase-scheme HTTP URLs like "HTTP://host/".
